summary: The agent completed a substantial, legitimate implementation and preserved baseline behavior, but failed 2 of 13 new tests because retention matched a reference token's symbolic owner directly instead of resolving inherited fields and methods to their actual declaring class.
quick_failure_summary: Inherited synthetic field and method declarations were omitted when emitted Java referenced them through a subclass.

details.reasoning: ReferenceRetentionContext.retainReferencesFrom constructs a GeneratedMemberKey directly from each FieldTextToken or MethodTextToken and only retains an exactly matching candidate. In the failing cases the emitted source uses Child.needed or Child.needed(), while the synthetic declaration belongs to Parent. Because the implementation never resolves the symbolic reference owner through the superclass/interface hierarchy, no Parent candidate matches and the required declaration stays hidden. This violates the stated requirement to declare a generated member when emitted Java refers to its declaration.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's added tests covered direct-owner references and many other requirements but did not cover inherited member resolution, so its full visible test run gave false confidence. This was a test-coverage gap, not cheating or an external execution failure.

justification.issue_description: References whose symbolic/source qualifier is a subclass must be resolved to the inherited field or method's actual declaring class before matching retention candidates.
justification.evidence: The prompt says, 'Declare each such member if the emitted Java of its file refers to it' and defines a reference as 'a use of a member by emitted Java code.' In the visible codebase, FieldExprent.getInferredExprType already walks cl.superClass until it finds the declaring StructField, and InvocationExprent's method lookup traverses superclasses and interfaces. The agent instead compared token owner/name/descriptor keys for exact equality. Hidden failures show emitted Child.needed and Child.needed() while the declarations are on Parent.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the general retention requirement explicitly covers every generated member referenced by emitted Java, and inherited lookup is ordinary Java behavior reinforced by visible repository code. The hidden tests reveal the defect but do not introduce an undocumented convention. This is more specifically a missed required case than a generic wrong-algorithm verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and architecturally demanding but solvable, as shown by the reference solution. The prompt clearly specifies file-wide, per-member, emitted-code-based fixed-point behavior and determinism. Inherited-reference resolution is a foreseeable consequence of Java member semantics, even though the prompt does not spell out inheritance as a separate example.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 3 baseline tests passed and all 13 new tests executed, with exactly 2 assertion failures and no errors or skips.
Both hidden failures occur during compilation of emitted Java because Child.needed or Child.needed() cannot be found; they meaningfully exercise the agent-modified retention logic.
The trajectory shows the agent successfully completed its focused tests and later a full ./gradlew :test run; there were no dependency, runtime, permission, network, API, or bootstrap failures.
A temporary JASM syntax error occurred while the agent authored its own fixture, but the agent corrected it and subsequently completed validation.
The verifier's initial 3-way test.patch merge failed, but its documented reset/reapply fallback succeeded and both suites ran, so this did not block or distort the result.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the hidden-test failures are explained by missing inherited-member resolution in the implementation.
